Class Game

java.lang.Object
chess.service.Game
public class Game extends Object
Coordinates a two-player game: owns the board, the players, and the turn, decides whether a requested move is allowed, and tracks check, checkmate, and stalemate.

This class contains no console or Swing code. The console version, the Swing GUI, the computer opponent, and the unit tests all call the same public methods. Interfaces that need to react to changes register a GameListener (Observer pattern).

Rules

  • All standard piece moves, including castling, en passant, and promotion to a queen, rook, bishop, or knight.
  • A move that leaves the mover's own king in check is rejected.
  • The game ends in checkmate (the side that delivered it wins) or stalemate (a draw). After that, every move is rejected until start() is called.
  • Not implemented: draws by threefold repetition, the 50-move rule, insufficient material, or agreement.

  • Method Details

    • start

      public final void start()
      Starts (or restarts) the game: sets up the board, clears history, gives White the first move, and notifies listeners. Declared final so a subclass cannot change what a restart means.

    • resetState

      private void resetState()
      Puts every field back to the starting position without notifying anyone. The constructor calls this instead of start(): notifying listeners from a constructor would hand out this before the object is fully built (javac's this-escape warning), and no listener could be registered yet anyway.

    • loadPosition

      public void loadPosition(Board setup, PieceColor toMove)
      Replaces the position with a custom one, for tests and demonstrations (for example, a stalemate position that would take many moves to reach). The move history is cleared and the status is recomputed for toMove.
      Parameters:
      setup - the position to copy; the game keeps its own copy
      toMove - the color whose turn it is

    • tryMove

      public MoveResult tryMove(Position from, Position to)
      Attempts to move the current player's piece from one square to another. A pawn reaching the last rank becomes a queen; use tryMove(Move) to choose.
      Parameters:
      from - source square; must not be null
      to - destination square; must not be null
      Returns:
      a MoveResult describing success or the reason for failure

    • tryMove

      public MoveResult tryMove(Move move)
      Attempts a move for the current player.

      If the game is over or MoveValidator.findProblem(Board, PieceColor, Move) finds a problem, the board, turn, and history are left exactly as they were and a failure is returned. Otherwise the move is applied, the turn passes, the status is recomputed (check, checkmate, stalemate), and every GameListener is notified.

      Parameters:
      move - the move to play; must not be null
      Returns:
      a MoveResult describing success or the reason for failure

    • computeStatus

      private GameStatus computeStatus()
      Works out the status for the player who is about to move.
      Returns:
      checkmate or stalemate if that player has no legal move, otherwise check or in-progress

    • describeMove

      private static String describeMove(Piece mover, Move move, MoveType type, Piece captured)
      Builds the sentence describing an accepted move, e.g. "Pawn E5 -> D6, capturing Black Pawn en passant".
      Parameters:
      mover - the piece that moved (before any promotion)
      move - the move played
      type - what kind of move it was
      captured - the captured piece, or null
      Returns:
      the description, without a final period
